subject.title: [Bug]: browser in docker hidden in cache folder

question: Should OpenClaw keep `/home/node/.cache/ms-playwright` as the Docker browser cache contract now that runtime autodetection exists, or migrate browser assets to `/opt` and expose `chrome`/`chromium` commands on PATH?
rationale: The remaining change affects Docker image defaults, persisted mounts, runtime install permissions, and command-surface expectations, so automation should not pick the product contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Keep current cache contract
options.body: Treat the merged Playwright cache autodetection as the fix for brittle versioned paths and close or redirect the `/opt` plus PATH request unless stronger migration evidence appears.

options.title: Approve `/opt` plus PATH migration
options.body: Require a focused Dockerfile/docs/test change with live proof for browser-enabled, browser-disabled, runtime-install, and existing-cache upgrade scenarios.

options.title: Narrow to PATH aliases only
options.body: Keep the current cache location but add layout-aware `chrome` and `chromium` commands only if maintainers want that Docker command surface.

recommendation.title: Keep current cache contract
recommendation.body: Treat the merged Playwright cache autodetection as the fix for brittle versioned paths and close or redirect the `/opt` plus PATH request unless stronger migration evidence appears.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete provided the prior same-repository close rationale for the Docker path migration and appears in adjacent Docker browser history as reviewer/merger.
